title: More than half of all mangrove ecosystems at risk of collapse by 2050, first global assessment finds
claim: IUCN's first global Red List assessment of mangrove ecosystems finds a majority at risk of collapse from deforestation, development, pollution, and sea-level rise, underscoring mangroves' critical role in coastal protection, carbon storage, and fishery support and the priority of restoring degraded stands.
evidence_text: IUCN's first global Red List of Ecosystems assessment of the world's mangroves found a majority of assessed mangrove ecosystems at risk of collapse, driven by deforestation, coastal development, pollution, altered freshwater and sediment flows from dam construction, and climate-driven sea-level rise. The assessment underscores mangroves' role in protecting coastal communities from flooding, storing carbon, and supporting fisheries, reinforcing native mangrove restoration and buffer replanting as a priority response where mangrove edges are degraded.
